chapter: Clubs, readers and musicians he knew
title: Hippolyte Charles, the Dutreys, Pico and the Moreira family
summary: He recalls Hippolyte Charles, Sam and Henry Dutrey, Alphonse Picou, Harrison Barnes in the Nola Band, and banjoist Lawrence Marrero and his brothers.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

Well, Hippolyte Chong. Oh, and I know him real good, too. He was a trumpet player, too. Yeah, he was sick, he got heart trouble, and he had a good plan. Yeah, I knew him good, too. And Sam and Henri Dutry. Oh, I know them good. I used to visit their home, Sam and Henri. Where did they live? Well, at that time, Sam had a pressing business on Anthony and Magazine, and they used to, the brothers used to be there kind of regular, you know, Henri and Peter there, and Sam. I used to go over there. You didn't work with them much? No, I worked with Sam a pretty good bit, but you know, he... His door band? Yeah, yeah, yeah, my band. What about Alphonse Pico? You must know him. Know him good, too, but I never did work with him. Somebody's talking to knock him off. Oh, that's gonna be my job. You must stop for a minute. What are you saying about Pico? How's Pico? I knew him good, but I never played with him, but I knew him very well. You know plenty of these people to somebody else. Like, you know, you meet somebody else, and they talk about people, and they introduce you, and you know them like that, but he was one of them. I knew him very well, but he was clarinet player. Alphonse was. Because he probably played saxophone later, I don't know, but I know he was clarinet player.

Yeah, he played way up until he died. Yeah. I read about a fellow named Duriam in a book. Did you ever hear of anybody called Duriam that played trombone? Duriam? No. Who was the trombone player with the Nola band then, other than Harrison Bond? Harrison Bond, yeah. Anybody else? No, I believe Harrison is the only one.

Yeah, Solomon was coming that door, yeah? All right. He left it open? No, he didn't open. Okay. Well, we can get it. Yeah. Well, I saw in a book about Duriam, and I never heard of anybody. I don't know that name at all. I don't know that name.
Did you ever know a fellow that played sousaphone named Booker? I know of him too, but I don't know him, Booker.

Booker Washington? Yeah, I don't know him. I know of him. What about Lawrence Muriero? Do you know him? Lawrence Muriero, I know him good as a book. He used to be a banjo player. He played with me. He did? In the Nola band? Yeah. Yeah, he played with the Nola band. Did you play with any of his relations too? Yeah. His brothers, Simon, what we call him, Simon Moreira, and Eddie. He played with you too? Well, no. He was in a different band. And John? John, yeah. John was with, for a long time he was with Tuxedo. Then he left town and went to New York and died.
I think he died about 1943. Oh, he was pretty good while ago.
